back: An API-aware reverse proxy that is the single entry point for clients and handles shared concerns.
Mapping public paths and versions to internal services, so they can change without clients noticing.
Sending a small share of traffic (e.g. 5%) to a new version and watching its errors.
Gateway authenticates (who are you?); services authorise (may you do this to this record?).
The gateway sets X-User-Id from the verified token and strips any client-sent copy.
Same for every service and needs no business data: TLS, auth, rate limits, logging, CORS.
One client call; the gateway fans out to several services in parallel and merges the results.
One client round trip plus the slowest parallel dependency, not the sum.
Per-dependency timeout plus a partial response.
Backend for frontend: one thin back end per client type, owned by that client's team.

front: Make the gateway not a SPOF?
back: Multiple stateless instances across zones, shared state in Redis, gradual config rollouts, keep it thin.
